0.0.n: Introduces the first step in the self-introduction.

0.3.n: This is the first part of 初めまして, a fixed greeting used when meeting someone new.

0.4.n: Completes 初めまして; this ending is not a separate word to translate here.

0.7.n: Links the opening greeting to the next step.

0.9.n: Refers to the name you will give in your introduction.

0.10.n: Marks 名前 as what you give; the verb is left unstated.

0.14.n: Politely ends the name statement; 〇〇 is a placeholder for your name.

1.1.n: This is a country name, placed before 出身 to identify your origin.

1.2.n: Follows a place name to indicate where someone originally comes from.

1.3.n: Makes the statement polite; the speaker leaves out 私は, meaning I.

2.1.n: This is a country name and the destination of 来る here.

2.2.n: Marks 日本 as the destination of coming.

2.3.n: The て-form of 来る links coming to Japan with the time elapsed since then.

2.5.n: 〇 stands for a number you supply, and 年 counts years.

2.6.n: Politely ends the elapsed-time statement; Japanese does not need a separate verb meaning has been here.

3.1.n: 〇 is a number placeholder; together with 前, this specifies how many years ago.

3.2.n: Follows a time amount to locate a point that far back from now.

3.3.n: Marks the starting point of the ongoing study.

3.4.n: 日本語 names the language being studied, not the country.

3.5.n: Marks 日本語 as what the speaker studies.

3.6.n: 勉強する becomes 勉強しています, a polite form showing study continuing from the stated starting point.

4.1.n: Names the language the speaker began studying.

4.2.n: Marks 日本語 as what the speaker began studying.

4.3.n: 勉強し combines with 始める to mean starting study; た makes it past tense.

4.4.n: Turns the preceding action into something that can serve as the sentence topic.

4.5.n: Marks the fact of starting study as the topic whose reason will be explained.

4.8.n: The plain form of です joins a noun or な-adjective reason to から.

4.9.n: Follows the reason; unlike the earlier から, this one explains a cause rather than a starting time.

4.10.n: Ends the reason-giving pattern からです politely.

0.lit: First, Nice to meet you. Then, your name: I am 〇〇.
0.tip: 初めまして is a fixed first-meeting greeting, and 〇〇です politely gives your name.

1.tip: Put a place before 出身です to say where you are originally from.

2.lit: To Japan having come, it is 〇 years.
2.tip: 来て〇年です expresses how many years have passed since arriving.

3.lit: Since 〇 years ago, Japanese have been studying.
3.tip: から gives the starting time, while しています shows that studying continues now.

4.lit: As for having started studying Japanese, it is because 〇〇.
4.tip: のは…からです frames an action as the topic and then explains its reason.
